source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
2. Give each failed check a distinct identification code or number to allow easy tracking and reference.

3. Indicate the date and time of the inspection during which the failure was noted as well as the name and credentials of the inspector.

4. Clearly specify the exact location within the building where the failed check occurred. Use floor plans or diagrams to pinpoint the area if necessary.

5. Document the nature of the non-compliance / failure observed. For example, lack of fire extinguishers, faulty sprinkler systems, blocked emergency exits, or malfunctioning fire alarms.

6. Attach photographs of the failed components or areas for visual documentation. Make sure the images are clear, well-lit, and clearly labeled with the location and date.

7. Include the relevant codes or regulations that were not met as a result of the failure. Cite applicable fire safety standards (such as NFPA, OSHA, or local fire department rules).

8. Note any
